body: Actually, I think a less hacky way to do this would be to create a theme item variation in the modern/classic themes that checks if the current theme is light.

> As for putting the color in a theme variation, I guess it'd work obviously, but these checkboxes are already under a theme variation:

Theme variations can inherit from other variations, so you would only need to do this:
```
p_theme->set_type_variation("[NewName]", "CheckBoxNoIconTint");
```
And that variation would then check if the theme is light and set the color. If dark, just leave it as is.

> And lastly, before committing this I did want to check if at least this hacky thing with the overbright colors has been used before, and it has! Found in `editor_audio_buses.cpp`:

Hacky stuff being used somewhere else isn't really a justification, as two wrongs don't make a right. :stuck_out_tongue:
Also, the bus example is very specific to that situation, while the checkbox visibility is a problem that could come up in other places, and it would be preferable to have a theme variation for consistency.

> Theme variations can inherit from other variations, so you would only need to do this:

Oh, didn't realize it was as simple as that! Changed it, thanks for the hint :]

> Hacky stuff being used somewhere else isn't really a justification, as two wrongs don't make a right.

True! Still, I don't see a way to keep the icon image itself light, without changing quite a bit of icon generation code just for this one exception.

<sub>But then again, I'm a beginner here sooooo maybe there is a way, I dunno</sub>
